hints: Focus on the two conditions in the question together, it must shift position to the right AND change the value of Kc.
Remember that for this reaction the forward direction is exothermic with $\Delta H^\ominus = -197 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so think how temperature affects an exothermic change.
Recall which single factor alone can change Kc, then link cooling to favouring heat release in the forward reaction to make more $\text{SO}_3$.
walkthrough:
**Recall what changes Kc**

Think of Kc as a number that only depends on temperature. Concentration, pressure and catalyst change the position, but they do not change Kc.

$$K_c = \frac{[\text{SO}_3]^2}{[\text{SO}_2]^2[\text{O}_2]}$$

**Decide the effect of temperature**

The forward reaction is exothermic, it gives out heat. Cooling the mixture removes heat, so Le Chatelier says the system replaces heat by moving forward to the right.

$$2\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(\text{g}) \quad \Delta H^\ominus < 0$$

**Link shift to Kc value**

Moving to the right by cooling means more $\text{SO}_3$ and less $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ at equilibrium. That makes the numerator bigger, so Kc gets larger. Only a temperature change does both jobs.

options.A: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally. It helps reach equilibrium faster but does not move the position and does not change Kc.
options.B: Increasing pressure does shift this equilibrium to the right because there are 3 moles of gas on the left and only 2 on the right. However, Kc stays the same, the concentrations adjust to keep Kc constant.
options.C: Decreasing temperature favours the exothermic direction, which is forward to make $\text{SO}_3$. This moves the position to the right and increases the value of Kc. It is the only change that does both.
options.D: Removing $\text{SO}_3$ does shift the position to the right to replace it. However, Kc is unchanged because the remaining concentrations re-adjust to give the same Kc value at the same temperature.
